newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 26.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The U.S. Supreme Court rejected a $1.3 billion settlement between asbestos manufacturers and about 100,000 people claiming injuries from the substance.

* The U.S. Supreme Court has upheld the Securities and Exchange Commission's contention that insider trading laws apply to people who have confidential information even if they have no connection to the company whose shares are being purchased.
* Wireless companies say they can't pay for billions of dollars of licenses won at auction and are vowing to default if the government does not restructure the debt.
* General Motors Corp is expected to offer average price increases of 1.3 percent on 1998 models, the smallest in 10 years.
* A government report says that hospital firms are getting help from Medicare in their quest over the past decade to takeover ailing hospitals.
* The U.S. Justice Department recommended that regulators rejected an application by Ameritech Corp to offer long-distance service in Michigan.
* The Dow Jones Industrials dropped 68.08 to close at 7689.98.
* OPEC extended a freeze on the cartel's production quotas until the end of the year.

* Liposome Co Inc saw its stock value plunge 62 percent in value after it reported that its drug candidate for lung inflammation showed no difference in patients taking the drugs and those given a placebo.
* Durable goods orders fell 0.6 percent in May.
* Personal computer consumers will find fewer choices this fall and during the holidays as retailers and manufacturers scale back because of weak demand.
* Andersen Worldwide's second nominee for the top job at the firm, George Shaheen, failed to secure the necessary partner votes to be elected.
* Boeing is experiencing shortages of thousands of aircraft parts and moderate delays in deliveries of some planes as it pushes toward record production levels.
* Granada Group Plc agreed to acquire the 73 percent of Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc it doesn't already own for about $1.2 billion.
* Heard on the Street: Westinghouse Electric Corp director and senior executive Mel Karmazin has scored points since taking control of the company's CBS TV station group.
* Credit Markets: Fixed-income investors are concerned about a surge of new bond issuance and new fears about inflation, prompting a late-day sell-off in the Treasury market.
